designSummary: Rapid review with an updated random-effects meta-analysis for the primary outcome when at least five trials report it.
sampleSize: The unit of analysis is the trial. The 2023 meta-analysis pooled nine trials for function; if the update adds two or three trials, a random-effects meta-analysis of about 11 trials and 1,200 participants gives a 95 percent confidence interval roughly 0.12 either side of the standardised mean difference, enough to separate a patient-important effect (0.3 or more) from little or no effect (below 0.2). With fewer than five trials reporting function the review will not pool.
primaryAnalysis: Random-effects meta-analysis (restricted maximum likelihood with the Hartung-Knapp adjustment) of standardised mean differences in function at about three months; certainty rated with GRADE.
secondaryAnalysis: Mean difference in daily steps; adherence and physiotherapist time summarised as medians and ranges across studies; qualitative findings grouped into themes; results for patients aged 75 or over extracted where reported.
missingData: No author contact in the time available; trials reporting only medians are included with a standard conversion and removed in a sensitivity analysis.
multiplicity: One primary outcome; secondary outcomes described with intervals and no significance testing.
software: R with the metafor package; screening log and extraction form kept in a dated shared workbook.
overfittingGuards: Pooling rule fixed before the search
No subgroup analysis beyond the pre-specified age split
Supplier-funded trials removed in one sensitivity analysis only
summary: Trial-level meta-analysis of function if five or more trials report it; about 11 trials would give an interval narrow enough for the decision.
